lines.trans: This is very good and fresh beef.
Lyova, try one more small piece.
Wait, chef, this is not beef after all.
Exactly, this is young tender veal!
You see, these Koreans are ordinary normal people.
They have some kind of special day today.
They are celebrating the birthday of their teacher.
Look, chef, what ordinary people they are!
It seems this is some very strange sect.

meanings.note: Adds a reason or an obvious truth. Core Russian part meaning 'after all, you know' in everyday speech.

Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: всякое бывает = all sorts of things happen
На всякий случай = just in case. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Что за глупости? = What nonsense?. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, foolishness' in everyday Russian.
Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'nonsense, foolishness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что за глупости? Значит, Осипенко сам эти деньги украл!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

Кажется as a parenthetical word. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to seem', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Koreans' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Diminutive of кусок. Common masculine noun meaning 'slice, little piece, bit' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Можно ещё кусочек? И шампанское можно выпить?

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.

examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'жный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('gentle, tender, delicate').

Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Standing out from others. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('special, particular').

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'мечать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'celebrate, mark'.

examples.text: Я не буду отмечать день рождения.
examples.trans: I will not celebrate my birthday.

examples.text: Я в этом году не буду шумно отмечать день рождения.

examples.text: Вся команда кухни собралась вечером отмечать общую победу.

meanings.note: impersonal, + dative: мне повезло = I was lucky; повезло! = what luck!

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be lucky (impersonal); to take (by vehicle)', paired with 'везти'.

examples.trans: A lucky break: Tretyakov called back.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

meanings.note: День рождения = birthday. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'birth' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Смотрите, врунишка новую машину купил! У врунишки сегодня день рождения!
examples.trans: Look, the little liar bought a new car! It's the little liar's birthday today!

meanings.note: Food, air, news. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екта'). Common feminine noun meaning 'sect / cult' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кажется, это какая-то очень странная секта.
examples.trans: It seems this is some very strange sect.

examples.text: Ладно, подожди меня здесь одну секунду.
examples.trans: Fine, wait for me here for one second.

examples.text: Я тебе сейчас один секрет скажу.
examples.trans: I will tell you one secret right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').
